name: Pigmentation Defects-Palmoplantar Keratoderma-Skin Carcinoma Syndrome
aliases: Pigmentation and Keratoderma with Skin Cancer Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse or focal palmoplantar keratoderma
Multiple pigmentation abnormalities including hypopigmented and hyperpigmented macules
Development of cutaneous carcinomas, particularly squamous cell carcinoma
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of palmoplantar keratoderma, pigmentation defects, and at least one skin carcinoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by genetic testing when available

laboratory: Histopathology of skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis and epidermal atypia
Genetic testing identifying mutations in keratin or pigmentation-related genes (if known)
imaging: Imaging for staging of skin carcinomas if invasive
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic triad of pigmentation defects, palmoplantar keratoderma, and skin carcinoma

distinguishingFeatures: Nail dystrophy without prominent pigmentation defects

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or ulcerating skin lesions suggestive of aggressive carcinoma
Early onset of multiple skin carcinomas before third decade
Family history of similar skin findings with malignant transformation
